paper.title: AgonAlpha: Autonomous Alpha Discovery via Prompt Economy and Scalable Agentic Search

evaluation_contract.interpretation: Platform-assigned metrics are stronger evidence than author-controlled backtests, but repeated adaptive search over the same evaluation window is not an untouched future-OOS test.

aggregate.independence_warning: The 60 submissions are adaptive tree-search outputs with shared evaluation feedback and must not be treated as 60 independent Bernoulli trials. The denominator also excludes the many internal candidate simulations performed before each submitted finalist.

paper_mechanisms.search_unit: complete research artifact: hypothesis, executable formula, evidence, rationale and verdict
paper_mechanisms.within_pipeline_selection: 16 -> 8 -> 4 -> 2 -> 1 halving tournament; nominal 31 evaluator calls before retries
paper_mechanisms.verification: fresh-context reviewer can re-execute evidence and veto verified fabrication, mismatch or leakage
paper_mechanisms.lineage: a candidate receives only selected ancestor reports rather than the complete global history
paper_mechanisms.scheduler: paper describes percentile reward, progressive widening, pending-aware UCB/backpressure and visit propagation
paper_mechanisms.future_validation: submitted alphas enter BRAIN OS tracking

upstream_public_framework.scope_note: The public repository identifies itself as the orchestration layer; data, evaluator integrations, generated candidates and results stay local and are not sufficient by themselves to recreate the paper deployment.

public_framework_parity_audit.paper_semantics: pending evaluations affect scheduler allocation so parallel workers do not repeatedly over-allocate the same lineage
public_framework_parity_audit.public_code_observation: scripts/mcts.py _ucb() uses completed child visits only; no pending-count term is present. cmd_next() returns the first existing pending candidate before creating another candidate.
public_framework_parity_audit.required_test: Run a deterministic multi-worker scheduler test proving unique concurrent allocations and paper-equivalent pending-count UCB semantics.

public_framework_parity_audit.paper_semantics: a completed node receives its percentile reward at completion and historical rewards are not recomputed as the population grows
public_framework_parity_audit.public_code_observation: _node_rewards() rebuilds percentile rewards from the current complete score history each time parent selection runs.
public_framework_parity_audit.required_test: Persist reward-at-completion and prove later completions do not retroactively change prior node rewards.

public_framework_parity_audit.paper_semantics: verified fabrication receives zero scheduler reward and is excluded from the percentile reference population
public_framework_parity_audit.public_code_observation: the scheduler state exposes only a finite numeric score and no explicit veto/exclusion state; a numeric zero would remain part of _score_history().
public_framework_parity_audit.required_test: Introduce an explicit invalid/veto state and prove invalid nodes neither earn reward nor alter the percentile population.

public_framework_parity_audit.paper_semantics: review includes evidence integrity plus sign logic, constant rationale, temporal stability and selection-risk diagnostics
public_framework_parity_audit.public_code_observation: the public generic alpha-reviewer prompt is centered on cheating/evidence consistency, rerun verification and leakage; it does not encode the full paper audit as mandatory output.
public_framework_parity_audit.required_test: Pin the exact experiment reviewer contract or reproduce the five audit dimensions as machine-readable checks.

methodological_limits: External evaluator independence reduces author-controlled backtest risk, but it does not remove adaptive multiple-testing risk when search repeatedly observes the same 2019-2023 evaluator window.
The paper reports entry into BRAIN OS tracking but not realized future OS performance, so durable future generalization remains unverified from the public paper evidence.
The headline 17/60 is a submitted-finalist success rate, not a raw candidate or evaluator-call hit rate; each normal 16-to-1 halving pipeline nominally performs 31 evaluations before retries.
Per-user SPECTACULAR rates range from 0% to 57.1% under different tree sizes and model routes, so the reported deployment does not causally isolate scheduler, reviewer or model contributions.

BRAIN is a proprietary evaluator. Public artifacts can establish consistency with returned platform evidence, but an independent third party cannot fully recompute the platform engine from the open repository alone.
The paper's sign-reflection shortcut depends on evaluator symmetry. It must not be copied into J-Quants after-cost/borrow experiments unless sign symmetry is directly verified.

issue194_implication.strongest_transferable_idea: Separate proposal from verification authority and make the evidence-bearing research artifact, not a formula string or chat transcript, the unit of search and lineage.
